inserts.wall_target.measured_on: owner decision of one project after a 2.5 mm wall with free space round it bulged when the inserts were melted in (0.6 nozzle, PETG, one printer); 4.0 itself is not confirmed by a print
inserts.wall_target.description: plastic round a heat-set pocket wherever the part has room

inserts.wall_floor.measured_on: insert makers give 1.3 to 1.6 for a straight hole of this size; not measured on a print
inserts.wall_floor.description: least plastic round a pocket even where a named neighbour stops the wall from growing

inserts.relief_wall_min.measured_on: decided, not measured by anybody: the only print behind it is 0.95 beside a relief that bulged (0.6 nozzle, PETG, one printer; the wall round the lead-in of that pocket was 2.5). Two values were in use in the project the rule comes from: "keep 2.5 beside the relief" (written after that print) and "cut a relief where 1.2 stays" (the value its relief tool cut with, and the one its pockets were made by). The stricter one is the default, computed, not measured: 4.0 round a D4.4 lead-in leaves 4.0 + 2.2 - 3.75 = 2.45 beside the D7.5 relief of the table, so a pocket that just meets inserts.wall_target with the full relief passes here. It is stricter than the 1.2 a project may have cut its reliefs by: such a project gets a row for every relief with 1.2 to 2.45 beside it until its owner sets the value (tag U or M)
inserts.relief_wall_min.description: plastic beside the melt relief, measured at the relief depth; also the wall a relief of the table must leave to count as fitting
inserts.relief_wall_min.x_note: One number serves two rules. In inserts.wall_at_relief a higher value is stricter. In inserts.relief_missing a higher value means fewer pockets where a relief counts as fitting: those rows turn from FAIL into BLOCKED and go to the owner, they never pass. A pocket whose wall round the lead-in is thin as well gets one row, from inserts.wall, that names the relief wall; inserts.wall_at_relief has the row of a pocket only when its walls pass or when a smaller relief of the table would fit.

inserts.relief_depth_min.measured_on: decided: a relief is whole layers deep, 0.54 = 3 layers of 0.18 was used (0.6 nozzle, PETG-CF, one printer)
inserts.relief_depth_min.description: a step at the mouth shallower than this is not a melt relief

inserts.relief_depth_max.measured_on: decided: every extra millimetre of relief costs thread engagement at stock screw lengths; 0.54 was in use
inserts.relief_depth_max.description: a relief is not deeper than this

inserts.floor_min.measured_on: decided, not measured on a print; 1.5 under a shortened pocket was also in use as a design figure for single parts
inserts.floor_min.description: plastic under the floor of a blind pocket; a pocket with less is cut through on purpose

inserts.iron_d.measured_on: decided: a soldering tip with its insert adapter; measure your own iron
inserts.iron_d.description: diameter of the straight path the iron needs in front of a pocket mouth

inserts.iron_reach.measured_on: decided: length of the tip and adapter in front of the handle
inserts.iron_reach.description: length of the free path in front of a pocket mouth

inserts.make.default: brass, spiral knurl, smooth pilot collar on top
inserts.make.measured_on: the insert shape the M3x4x5 row of the table was measured with; a project names its own make
inserts.make.description: insert make and shape the pocket table is valid for

inserts.ref_pattern.measured_on: naming habit of one project; set it to how insert refs are named. A ref the pattern does not match is not seen as the thread of a screw
inserts.ref_pattern.description: a ref body whose name matches is a heat-set insert

rules.title: Every heat-set pocket has a known profile
rules.statement: A hole whose diameters fall in the band of an insert kind of rules/tables/inserts.json has exactly the pocket profile of that kind: melt relief, lead-in, hole, depth. The profile is cut by the shared pocket tool from the table, never typed into a part script. A pocket shortened for a thin part is a named exception, not a second profile.
rules.why: Three pocket shapes that were not the measured one were printed. A lead-in as wide as the knurl let the inserts drop 65 % of their length in cold and grip weakly. A straight datasheet hole came out loose once the slicer hole compensation was on: inserts pulled out by hand with a screw, and every pocket of the project was converted. A hole tuned on full parts took five re-exports in one day. The old check listed only pockets that already had the right shape, so a wrong pocket was never a row.
fix_order: Cut the pocket again from the table with the shared pocket tool, together with its relief.
A kind with no measured row: print a coupon in the final filament first (inserts.coupon_first), then add the row.
If the hole is not an insert pocket, answer the question "what is this hole" once.
rules.note: A blind hole that is a pocket for a bought part at the size of its fit parameter (rules/tables/pockets.json: today the magnet) is not judged here, whatever insert band its diameter lies in: fits.bought_part_pocket judges it. A hole that holds an insert or a screw (a ref on its axis that inserts.ref_pattern or screws.ref_pattern names) is never such a pocket. A pocket whose relief was cut later ends one relief depth short of its row: that is a row here, and its text names the cause (the row was measured with its full depth; the table's "hole_short_by_relief" would allow it, a decision that no print measured, so it is false as shipped). A narrower hole below the pocket (a tip hole, the screw hole from the far side) is depth, as long as the insert itself ends in the row's own hole diameter. A through hole with the pocket at each end is two pockets. The insert ref on the axis decides the kind: a longer insert in the pocket of the short one is a wrong pocket. A hole too short to hold the insert at all is one row of inserts.floor, not a row here.

rules.title: Plastic round a heat-set pocket
rules.statement: Round every heat-set pocket the plastic is at least {inserts.wall_target} wherever the part has room, at the lead-in and along the insert. The wall is measured to the first way out of the plastic: an outside face, another pocket, a hole or a cavity, also one cut from the opposite face. Less is allowed only where a named neighbour stops the wall, with the owner's waiver, and never under {inserts.wall_floor}. Every pocket under the target is a row: FAIL under the floor, GROW with free space, BLOCKED by a named neighbour. There is no pass value below the target.
rules.why: A 2.5 mm wall with free space on every side passed a check written as "at least the floor value" and bulged when the inserts were melted in, on a large printed part. In another part the pockets of two joints met inside the plastic with a 0.1 mm web between them (found in the model).
fix_order: Where the outline of the part is free on that side, make the whole wall, shoulder or lap wider: one flat face, no islands.
Move the pocket together with its screw hole in the mating part and its hardware refs.
A local boss only where the outline cannot move, with the reason named.
Blocked on every side: report it with the neighbour that stops the wall and ask the owner for a waiver.
rules.note: Free space can be a motion or assembly path: a part that turns past, a motor that is slid in. The probe sees bodies, not paths: prove the space with a sweep or a dry run before growing into it. Run the check again after any relief or landing cut: the lead-in moves down with the face. One pocket gives one row for its walls: when the wall beside the relief is thin too, this row names it and inserts.wall_at_relief says nothing (unless a smaller relief of the table would fit: then that rule has the row and names this wall). A relief wall that is thin for a reason of its own, thinner than this wall and the step between the two diameters explain, is a second finding: inserts.wall_at_relief has a row for it besides the row here. A pocket with no relief where none fits for want of wall is named in this row as well. A pocket the insert probe did not measure (the tables changed after the facts were collected; the far end of a post with a pocket at each end) is NOT_RUN here.
supersedes: a wall of at least the floor value as the design value
a pass value below the target
a boss as the first or standard fix

rules.title: Plastic beside the melt relief
rules.statement: Beside the melt relief, at the relief depth, at least {inserts.relief_wall_min} of plastic stays. Where a neighbour stops the wall, the relief steps down through the fallback diameters of the table before the wall gets thinner than that.
rules.why: 0.95 mm was left beside a relief on a pocket whose lead-in wall was 2.5 mm, and it bulged. The wall check measured along the insert only, and the thin-wall check on the STL hid rims round pockets.
fix_order: Use the next smaller relief diameter of the table.
Where the outline of the part is free on that side, make the whole wall, shoulder or lap wider: one flat face, no islands.
Move the pocket together with its screw hole in the mating part and its hardware refs.
A local boss only where the outline cannot move, with the reason named.
Blocked on every side: report it with the neighbour that stops the wall and ask the owner for a waiver.
rules.note: Two values were written down for this wall: 2.5 after the print that bulged, and 1.2 as the point where the relief steps down. The registry holds one parameter with the stricter value (see its measured_on for the exact figure). A pocket squeezed beside a seat, where only a smaller wall is possible, is a BLOCKED row for the owner. One pocket gives one row for its walls: this rule has it when the walls round the lead-in pass, and when a smaller relief of the table would fit while the wall is not under its floor. A relief wall that is thin for a reason of its own (0.2 mm towards the relief of the next pocket while the lead-in wall is 3.3: thinner than that wall and the step between the two diameters explain) is a row here besides the row of inserts.wall: two causes, two rows, so the worst wall of a pocket is never only a text. In every other case the row is the one of inserts.wall, which names the wall beside the relief.
supersedes: 1.2 beside the relief as the default

rules.title: Plastic under a blind pocket
rules.statement: Under the floor of a blind pocket at least {inserts.floor_min} of plastic stays, or the pocket is through on purpose. An insert is never longer than the material it sits in.
rules.why: A hub was too thin for its pocket and a paper-thin skin was left under it. An insert longer than its plate pokes out of the other face.
fix_order: Make the part thicker under the pocket, and what sits on it.
Use a shorter insert with its own table row.
Cut the pocket through on purpose.
rules.note: The row of a hole that is too short for its insert is this rule's alone: the shape and wall rules say nothing about such a hole. When the census read only a short piece of the hole with an open wall (a radial pocket that ends in a curved bore, a hole cut by a slit), nothing was measured and the row is NOT_RUN: look at the hole in the model.

rules.title: Every pocket has its melt relief
rules.statement: Every heat-set pocket is cut together with a melt relief at its mouth: a step of a relief diameter of the table, {inserts.relief_depth_min} to {inserts.relief_depth_max} deep (whole layers), on the face the mating part lands on, wherever a relief diameter of the table leaves {inserts.relief_wall_min} beside it. The insert ends flush with the relief floor. A pocket with no relief is a row on every face, the bed face included. A pocket at the bottom of a recess (a spot face, a counterbore) needs its relief in the floor of that recess: the recess is not the relief.
rules.why: A large part was printed with a dozen pockets and no relief: the ring of plastic each insert pushed up held the mating part off its face. More than fifty pockets in nine other parts were the same. The rule had existed for three weeks but was only a report, the detector took a wall on one side of a pocket for a relief, and a pocket conversion had dropped reliefs. Later a pocket in a spot face read as relieved, because any wide first step counted as a relief.
fix_order: Cut the relief with the shared pocket tool. A new pocket is never cut "relief later".
Run the wall checks again: the lead-in moved down by the relief depth, and a pocket from the opposite face may now be too close.

No relief diameter of the table leaves the wall: the row goes to the owner as one decision for the group. He chooses a smaller relief with less beside it, or no relief with the bench line "shave the melt ring" (inserts.noroom_bench).
rules.note: A pocket with no relief where no relief of the table fits is a BLOCKED row here only when its walls round the lead-in pass. When they are thin, the row of inserts.wall names the missing relief: one pocket, one row.
supersedes: bed-face reliefs may be left out
tight pockets keep no relief and are not counted

rules.title: The iron reaches every pocket mouth
rules.statement: In front of every pocket mouth a straight path {inserts.iron_d} wide and {inserts.iron_reach} long is free of the part itself. An insert is set on the bench, in the bare part: a neighbour that is mounted later does not count. A through hole with a pocket at each end has two mouths; a straight through pocket takes its insert from either end and fails only when the part closes both. No pocket is sealed. Prefer a face that is a top face in the print.
rules.why: The insert mouths of a clamp ended up under a collar wall (reported by the owner), and one pocket on a lug was sealed where no iron could reach it.
fix_order: Turn the pocket to a face that is open.
Open a window in what covers the mouth.
A neighbour in front of the mouth is no finding of this rule: write into the build notes that the insert is set before that part is mounted.

rules.title: One pocket table for every project
rules.statement: Pocket sizes come from one shared table keyed by insert kind (rules/tables/inserts.json). A project uses them and does not copy the numbers. Each fastener-in-plastic kind a project uses (every insert size, a thread-forming pilot, a wood screw) has its own row: hole, depth, relief. A kind whose row is not measured is not used in a part until its coupon is printed, and a project changes a row only when a print in its own filament and nozzle measured otherwise.
rules.why: Pocket numbers typed into part scripts drifted apart: four counterbore and three pocket generations were found in one model. The long M3 and the M5 pockets of that model still follow the straight-hole logic that failed for the measured kind.
rules.note: The shape of each pocket is checked by inserts.pocket_shape.

rules.title: A pocket size is trusted only after its coupon
rules.statement: Before a pocket size goes into parts, print a coupon in the final filament and nozzle: a small block with 4 to 7 pockets, the hole size engraved by each (about 10 g, 25 minutes). The right pocket lets a cold insert drop only as deep as its pilot band and then needs heat. After install, pull on the insert by hand with a screw in it. A result in one material does not carry to another: PLA prints holes small and hides a loose pocket.
rules.why: A pocket "validated" in a PLA fit test was loose in the carbon-filled parts: an insert came out by hand with a screw.
rules.note: Asked per part through fits.decided_not_printed: a kind with tag D in the table is a fit that was never printed.

rules.title: A moved face takes its pockets with it
rules.statement: Pocket depth is measured from its face. When a face with pockets is moved, filled, offset or cut (a clamp landing, a spot face, a relief), the pockets and their reliefs are cut again from the new face in the same pass, the wall checks are run again and the insert refs are moved with them.
rules.why: A landing cut 1.0 deeper removed the reliefs of the pockets in it and left the hardware refs at the old height. Dozens of insert refs stood 0.54 too high, which also shifted every engagement number read from them.
rules.note: Caught on the next run by inserts.relief_missing, inserts.pocket_shape and regression.feature_lost.

rules.title: No load-bearing thread cut in the print
rules.statement: A screw that is tightened against a load or adjusted again goes into a heat-set insert, a nut or a bought thread, never into a thread cut or formed in the print. A thread-forming pilot is allowed only for a rarely turned, lightly loaded screw, as a named exception.
rules.why: A D2.6 hole tapped in a printed part came out oval and the plastic thread stripped.

attest.question: Hole {feature}: a thread in the print. Which screw goes in, and why not an insert?
labels: rarely turned, lightly loaded screw: a named exception, listed in the report for the owner
not a thread: a pin, dowel, magnet or alignment hole of that size

rules.note: Judged from the census: every hole of tap-drill size (screws table) or in a pilot band (inserts table) is asked once per hole. A screw whose shank lies in solid plastic is screws.hole_through.

rules.title: Inserts are installed against a stop
rules.statement: An insert is melted in against a stop: a screw and a flat washer on the insert, so it ends flush with the relief floor. Inserts go in before a bearing is pressed in beside them. A loose insert is rescued with two-part epoxy, the same stop and a greased screw, not with superglue: it is brittle and wicks into the thread. A printed part that fails the wall rule gets a written work-around for the bench: melt its inserts last and briefly.
rules.why: Inserts that stood proud under a clamp face held the mating parts apart: one of three suspected causes of 2 mm of play in a built joint.

rules.title: The relief is sized by the install stop
rules.statement: The relief diameter is the stop washer of the install plus clearance. The full relief takes a normal flat washer, the first fallback a small-series washer, and the last one has no stop: the insert is pushed 0.5 below the face by eye. The table lists the stop of each diameter. The relief is not deeper than {inserts.relief_depth_max}: every extra millimetre costs thread engagement at stock screw lengths.
rules.why: No failed print of its own: it is why the relief diameters are what they are. A relief narrower than the stop washer lets the washer land on the face, and the insert ends proud by the relief depth.

rules.title: A pocket with no room for a relief is shaved at the bench
rules.statement: A pocket where no relief diameter of the table leaves {inserts.relief_wall_min}, typically a clamp-washer pocket close to a bearing seat, keeps no relief only by the owner's decision. The melt ring it leaves is shaved flush with a countersink or a knife after install, and that step is written in the build notes of the part. Where a washer heels on the same landing, the ring is gone before the washer goes on.
rules.why: About two dozen such pockets were listed by the old check and not counted. A ring left on a washer landing tilts the washer, and neither a check nor a bench step said so.
rules.note: The rows come from inserts.relief_missing (BLOCKED). See also washers.landing_melt_ring.

rules.title: The project names its insert make
rules.statement: The pocket table is valid for one insert make and shape: {inserts.make}. The project names its make, and every purchase is checked against it. A straight or diamond knurl of the same nominal size needs its own coupon.
rules.why: Straight-knurl inserts of the same nominal size were put into a shopping cart for pockets measured with a spiral knurl and a pilot collar. It was caught before the order.

rules.title: Reserve pockets on a long print
rules.statement: A long, expensive print may carry reserve insert pockets for a likely future interface where they cost nothing. They follow every pocket rule, and inserts that stay unused are named as such in the hardware refs.
rules.why: No failed print behind it: an owner decision on one large part, so that a later mount does not need a reprint.
